facts.claim: Bioko island covers 2,017 km2 and, according to INEGE, was called Fernando Poo during Spanish colonisation in honour of the Portuguese navigator who discovered it in 1472.

source.title: Annuaire Statistique de la Guinée Équatoriale 2025
source.publisher: INEGE (Instituto Nacional de Estadística de Guinea Ecuatorial)
source.quote: dont 2 017 km² correspondent à l'île de Bioko ... Elle a été appelée Fernando Poo pendant la colonisation espagnole, en l'honneur du navigateur portugais qui l'a découverte en 1472

facts.claim: Bioko is ringed by a coastal plain about 5 km wide, which holds three bays, one of them the bay of the port of Malabo.

source.title: Annuaire Statistique de la Guinée Équatoriale 2025
source.publisher: INEGE (Instituto Nacional de Estadística de Guinea Ecuatorial)
source.quote: L'île est entourée d'une plaine côtière d'environ 5 kilomètres de large ... celle du port de Malabo, celle de La Concepción et celle de Luba

facts.claim: A presidential decree of January 2026 declared Ciudad de la Paz, in Djibloho province, the capital of Equatorial Guinea in place of Malabo.

source.title: E.Guinea relocates capital to 'city of peace'
source.quote: Ciudad de la Paz, in the province of Djibloho, is declared the capital of the Republic of Equatorial Guinea

facts.claim: Malabo is described as a city of about 300,000 people on Bioko Island, which official institutions were given a year to leave after the 2026 capital decree.

source.title: Equatorial Guinea's new capital still has no residents
source.quote: Official institutions have been given a year to move from the old capital Malabo, a city of about 300,000 on Bioko Island in the Gulf of Guinea.

facts.claim: Malabo was the capital from independence from Spain in 1968 until the 2026 decree.

source.title: Equatorial Guinea's new capital still has no residents
source.quote: Malabo had been the capital since independence from Spain in 1968

facts.claim: The British called the settlement Port Clarence and it was later named Santa Isabel in honour of the Queen of Spain.

source.title: Aldaba (UNED) article on Spain and Equatorial Guinea
source.quote: Fue llamada por los ingleses Port Clarence y posteriormente, Santa Isabel en honor de la reina de España

facts.claim: The expansion of Malabo has deepened uneven urban planning, producing neighbourhoods with large social differences and poor connections, according to the Spanish cultural centre in the city.

source.title: Plan de Centro 2023, Centro Cultural de España en Malabo
source.publisher: AECID, Centro Cultural de España en Malabo
source.quote: El proceso expansivo de Malabo ha acuciado la desigual articulación urbanística, dando lugar a barrios con grandes diferencias sociales y mal conectados.

facts.claim: INEGE's yearbook tracks air traffic at the airport of Malabo and the arrival of commercial ships at the ports of Malabo and Bata.

source.title: Annuaire Statistique de la Guinée Équatoriale 2025

facts.claim: Rapid urban growth of Malabo, the former political capital on Bioko island, and of Bata was among the reasons cited for moving the capital.

source.title: Ciudad de la Paz devient la nouvelle capitale de la Guinée équatoriale
source.quote: la croissance urbaine rapide des villes de Malabo (ex-capitale politique située sur l’île de Bioko) et Bata

places.name: Monte Alén National Park
places.what: Monte Alén National Park, established in 1990 on the mainland, covers about 2,000 km2 and shelters central chimpanzees and western lowland gorillas among 15 to 16 primate species. Monte Alén and Monte Mitra, at about 1,250 m, are thought to be the highest massifs of mainland Equatorial Guinea.

places.name: Catedral de Santa Isabel de Malabo
places.what: This neo-Gothic cathedral with three naves was built between 1897 and 1916, with two 40-metre towers finished in 1924. A fire destroyed its roof in January 2020 while it was closed for restoration; a link to Gaudí is not supported by any known document.

source.title: Another Gaudí’s work in Africa?
source.quote: The monument was erected between 1897 and 1916 ... It is a neo-Gothic church with three naves with a Latin cross plan inscribed in a rectangle.

source.title: Another Gaudí’s work in Africa?
source.quote: there were still the two 40-meter-tall towers to be built on the facade, finished in 1924

source.title: Another Gaudí’s work in Africa?
source.quote: Gaudí’s intervention is not supported by any known document.

myth.claim: Antoni Gaudí designed or approved the cathedral of Malabo.
myth.truth: Several publications said Gaudí advised the designer, but the Gaudí Foundation states that no known document supports any intervention by him; the monument was built between 1897 and 1916 by the Claretian missionary Luis Sagarra Llauradó.

source.title: Another Gaudí’s work in Africa?
source.quote: Gaudí’s intervention is not supported by any known document.
